I recall the moment when my Zulip inbox became a labyrinth of threads, mentions, and urgent queries—an endless stream of messages from creditors, legal advisors, committee members, and other IBC stakeholders. Discussions about claim verifications would be in one stream, updates on NCLT hearings in another, and somewhere else, a crucial timeline for asset valuation or EOI publication would be buried. Each day became a scavenger hunt: sift through Zulip, switch to Taiga to update the CIRP or liquidation timeline, add compliance tasks, and hope nothing critical slipped through the cracks. It was draining—and, as every insolvency professional knows, the stakes for missing a deadline or miscommunicating with stakeholders are high[5][6][11].

That’s when I decided: enough chaos, let’s build something better.

Where We Started

As an insolvency professional, I rely heavily on asynchronous communication. Stakeholders—Committee of Creditors (CoC), suspended directors, valuers, legal teams—are scattered across cities and time zones. Zulip’s structured chat is great for context, but as the process grows, keeping conversations in sync with the statutory timelines and compliance requirements in Taiga becomes a nightmare. I found myself constantly copying links, searching for the latest IA status or CoC decision, or simply losing track of whether a compliance affidavit was filed on time. The risk of missing a CIRP-7 filing or an SCC consultation was real[5][8][11].

A Painful Reality

For every new issue—be it a claim dispute, an IA filed by a promoter, or a new compliance requirement—the same pattern emerged:

  • Someone flagged an issue in Zulip.
  • We’d discuss solutions, sometimes over days, with key points lost in the chat.
  • Eventually, someone would realize: this needs to be tracked in Taiga.
  • By then, crucial details were stuck in Zulip threads, inaccessible to new team members or those responsible for statutory filings.
  • Deadlines were missed, compliance gaps emerged, or the same query was answered multiple times because context was scattered.

The Spark of Inspiration

We started brainstorming: what if Zulip and Taiga could “talk” to each other in real-time? What if an AI agent could monitor Zulip streams, extract actionable items, and update Taiga automatically? But why stop there? Why not build a “Scrum Master” agent—an IBC process coordinator—that could:

  • Check Zulip for daily updates, IA discussions, or compliance reminders.
  • Create and update tasks in Taiga for every statutory event—claim verifications, CoC meetings, CIRP-7 filings, SCC consultations—without manual intervention.
  • Summarize multi-day stakeholder conversations and flag items needing status changes.
  • Prompt team members for daily blockers or compliance risks, and compile meeting notes for the record.
  • Ensure that no compliance deadline, stakeholder update, or critical document is missed due to fragmented communication.

Building the IBC Scrum Agent

At first, it seemed simple: connect a Zulip bot to the Taiga API, set up a few triggers, and automate repetitive updates. But the complexity of insolvency processes quickly became clear:

  • Multiple “Brains” (Agents): One to summarize Zulip chats, another to interact with Taiga’s APIs, and another to monitor compliance calendars and statutory filings.
  • Context-Aware Architecture: The agent needed to remember which IA related to which CIRP stage, who was responsible for each compliance, and which stakeholder group needed what update.
  • Supervisor Layer: With so many moving parts—legal, financial, operational—the agent needed a conductor, orchestrating sub-agents to prevent missed filings or duplicated efforts.

Despite the technology, the principle was simple: keep stakeholder communication flowing in Zulip, while ensuring Taiga always reflects the true state of the process, compliance, and statutory timelines.

The Core Problem We’re Solving

Insolvency processes are plagued by information fragmentation and procedural complexity[5][6][11]. Before this agent, aligning chatty stakeholder discussions with the structured, statutory world of Taiga required constant manual effort. Critical filings could be missed, SCC consultations delayed, or CoC decisions lost in the shuffle. The agent bridges this gap, ensuring every compliance task, deadline, and stakeholder update is tracked, recorded, and actioned in real time.

Personal Wins and Nightmares

Early versions had their quirks—reminding the team about CIRP-7 filings at odd hours, or creating new Taiga tasks for every mention of “claim” or “IA” in Zulip. But with each iteration, the agent became smarter, filtering noise, mapping conversations to compliance events, and drastically reducing the overhead for daily updates and statutory filings.

How You Can Use It

  • Keep Everyone on Track: The agent organizes statutory events, compliance tasks, and stakeholder updates, so no one scrambles to find the latest status.
  • Unified Search: Search Zulip and Taiga together—catch up on stakeholder discussions, track IA statuses, or review compliance history in one place.
  • Compliance Automation: The agent prompts for daily compliance checks, compiles summaries for the record, and ensures filings are never missed.
  • Cross-Referencing: If a Zulip conversation reaches a compliance threshold, the agent creates or updates a Taiga task—no more toggling between chat and project board.

Looking Ahead

The IBC Scrum Agent is just beginning. Next steps include:

  • Integration with other platforms: For teams using Slack, WhatsApp, or email, the agent will bridge those channels too.
  • Jira and Legal Database Compatibility: Extend automation to other project management and legal research tools.
  • Deeper Analytics: Track repeated compliance bottlenecks, generate reports on process delays, and highlight risks for stakeholders.
  • Enhanced Memory: Maintain a record of all communications, filings, and decisions across months for audit and transparency.

Wrapping Up

For insolvency professionals, the cost of miscommunication or missed deadlines is high—potentially derailing the entire process and risking professional liability[6][11]. Building this agent was born out of frustration with fragmented tools and the desire for a single, reliable source of truth. With each improvement, we move closer to a world where every stakeholder is informed, every compliance is tracked, and the insolvency process is as smooth and transparent as possible.

If you’re tired of juggling chat, timelines, and compliance across scattered tools, the IBC Scrum Agent is here to help. Let’s bring order to the chaos—so you can focus on resolving insolvency, not managing information overload.
